tags.gist: Notes the paper's proposals have mature drug-side analogues, and says new vocabulary for the same mechanisms costs sponsors who work across centers.
Asks FDA to explain how the competency approach applies to GenAI functions in combination products led by another center, with one shared risk vocabulary.
Asks sponsors to state in advance how they weigh under- and over-escalation, show performance across the trade-off, and justify the chosen operating point.
Would describe the two axes with FDA's existing terms, model influence and decision consequence, or state that they mean the same thing.
Wants the resulting risk tier to set the evidence level, giving sponsors one assessment that serves both premarket planning and later change control.
Calls the ten benchmarking elements helpful and generally well designed.
Would add an element defining the test article and full configuration, with the marketed version matching it and setting changes triggering re-benchmarking.
Would tie element E.4 to FDA's human factors framework and clarify whether its evidence can come from a human factors validation study.
Wants provenance dating and canary items for public benchmarks, a prespecified construction plan for sponsor benchmarks, and sequestered holdout data for higher-risk functions.
Would have third parties qualify and maintain benchmark suites through MDDT, with requalification intervals and structural independence, rather than certify devices.
Wants monitoring plans to specify parameters, sampling, alert and action limits and responses before authorization, with premarket results as the trending baseline.
Would categorize changes by which benchmarking elements they could affect, agreed prospectively in a PCCP as drug change protocols do.
Wants an inventory of irreversible actions each gated by human confirmation no model can satisfy, plus audit records that let any interaction be reconstructed.
Supports the direction and mainly asks CDRH to reuse existing FDA tools and terminology, from risk terms to change protocols and action limits.
